name: Opening Script (All Calls)
description: A standardized call center script used by agents at the start of every customer interaction to establish a professional greeting and perform initial security verification.
context: Good morning/afternoon. You've reached FirstUK Bank.
For security, may I have the last 4 digits of your account number and your date of birth?
I've confirmed your details. Let me help you with [reason].

name: Customer Name
description: A dynamic placeholder used by the agent to personalize the greeting after the customer has provided their name.
context: Thank you, [Customer Name]. How can I help you today?

name: Reason for Call
description: A placeholder representing the specific issue or request the customer is calling about, used to close the verification phase and begin the service phase.
context: Let me help you with [reason].

name: Customer Identity Verification Obligation
description: The requirement for agents to verify a customer's identity using specific security markers (last 4 digits of account number and date of birth) before proceeding with the request.
context: For security, may I have the last 4 digits of your account number and your date of birth?
[Verify against system]

name: Bank Customer
description: The individual contacting FirstUK Bank who must undergo security verification before receiving assistance.
context: [Customer provides name]
[Customer explains reason for call]

name: Customer Account
description: The customer's bank account, the last four digits of which are used as a security verification token.
context: may I have the last 4 digits of your account number

name: Account Opening Inquiry Agent Script
description: A call centre script used by agents to guide customers through the process of opening a SmartSaver account. It outlines the product benefits, interest rates, and the three available application methods (online, branch, and post).
context: Agent: "Excellent choice! Our SmartSaver account offers some of the best interest rates available."
We have three ways to open an account: 1. Online... 2. In one of our 12 branches... 3. By post
Do you have any questions about the SmartSaver?

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A savings product offering interest rates between 4.50% and 4.80% AER with no monthly fees.
context: I'd like to open a SmartSaver account.
Our SmartSaver account offers some of the best interest rates available.
We currently offer 4.50% to 4.80% AER depending on your balance, with no monthly fees.

name: New Customer
description: An individual inquiring about and intending to open a new banking product with FirstUK Bank.
context: Customer: "I'd like to open a SmartSaver account."
Which option works best for you?

name: SmartSaver Account Opening
description: The process of establishing a new SmartSaver account via online, branch, or postal channels.
context: We have three ways to open an account
Our staff will help you open the account on the spot.

name: SmartSaver Identity and Address Verification
description: The requirement for customers opening accounts online to provide specific government-issued identification and proof of residency.
context: You'll need a UK Passport or Driving License, plus proof of address (utility bill, council tax, or bank statement).
The process takes about 10 minutes.

name: Interest Rate Question Agent Script
description: A call centre script designed to explain to customers why their SmartSaver interest rate has decreased, linking the change to the Bank of England's base rate and the bank's fixed margin.
context: Agent: "Great question. Our SmartSaver rates are variable, which means they move with the Bank of England's base rate."
We maintain a fixed 2.5% margin above the BoE rate, so your rate always stays competitive.

name: Current Interest Rate
description: A dynamic field in the agent script representing the customer's specific current interest rate expressed as AER.
context: Your current rate is 4.50% AER.

name: SmartSaver
description: A variable-rate savings product that tracks the Bank of England's base rate with a fixed margin.
context: Our SmartSaver rates are variable
We maintain a fixed 2.5% margin above the BoE rate

name: SmartSaver Customer
description: An existing bank customer inquiring about changes to their account interest rates.
context: Customer: "Why did my interest rate drop?"

name: Failed Transaction Agent Script
description: A call centre script designed to guide agents through the process of investigating and resolving a customer's failed transfer. It provides a structured approach to gathering transaction details and offering specific resolutions based on the failure reason.
context: Agent: "I'm sorry to hear that. Let me look into this for you."
The transfer failed because [reason: insufficient funds/invalid recipient/account closed/other].
Here's what we can do: [Offer resolution based on scenario]

name: Transfer Attempt Date
description: A dynamic data point the agent must collect from the customer regarding when the failed transfer was attempted.
context: When did you attempt the transfer?

name: Transfer Amount
description: A dynamic data point the agent must collect from the customer regarding the monetary value of the failed transfer.
context: How much was it for?

name: Recipient Account
description: The destination account details for the failed transfer that the agent must verify with the customer.
context: To which account?

name: Failure Reason
description: The specific cause of the transaction failure, such as insufficient funds, invalid recipient, or a closed account.
context: [reason: insufficient funds/invalid recipient/account closed/other]

name: Resolution Offer
description: A conditional response provided by the agent based on the specific reason the transaction failed.
context: [Offer resolution based on scenario]

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who is reporting a failed transfer and interacting with the agent.
context: Customer: "My transfer didn't go through."

name: Customer Account
description: The account held by the customer which the agent must check to identify the cause of the failed transfer.
context: Let me check your account... [Pull transaction record]

name: Failed Transfer Transaction
description: A financial transfer event that did not complete successfully, serving as the trigger for the customer interaction.
context: My transfer didn't go through.
The transfer failed because [reason: insufficient funds/invalid recipient/account closed/other].

name: Fraud/Unauthorized Transaction Agent Script
description: A call centre script used by agents to handle customers reporting unauthorized transactions. It guides the agent through empathy, data collection, immediate mitigation steps, and setting expectations for investigation and refund timelines.
context: Agent: "I'm very sorry to hear that. We take fraud seriously and will investigate immediately."
"I'm going to: 1. Block any suspicious transactions right away 2. Investigate what happened 3. Refund you within 10 days"
"We'll follow up with you within 5 business days with our findings."

name: Unauthorized Transaction Details
description: Dynamic information provided by the customer regarding the specific fraudulent event, including which transaction, the date of occurrence, and the amount.
context: Which transaction is unauthorized?
When did it occur?
How much was it for?

name: Customer Contact Phone Number
description: The phone number provided by the customer for the bank to use when following up with the findings of the fraud investigation.
context: Is there a phone number where we can reach you?

name: Immediate Blocking of Suspicious Transactions
description: The requirement for the agent to immediately stop any further suspicious financial activity on the account once fraud is reported.
context: I'm going to: 1. Block any suspicious transactions right away

name: Fraud Investigation and Refund Timeline
description: The obligation to investigate the reported unauthorized transaction and provide a refund within a 10-day window if the fraud is confirmed.
context: Investigate what happened
Refund you within 10 days if the transaction is confirmed as unauthorized

name: Fraud Investigation Follow-up Deadline
description: The commitment to contact the customer with the results of the fraud investigation within 5 business days.
context: We'll follow up with you within 5 business days with our findings.

name: Fraud Victim Customer
description: A customer who has identified and reported a transaction on their account that they did not authorize.
context: Customer: "I see a transaction I didn't authorize."

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: A financial transaction reported by the customer as not being authorized by them, triggering a fraud investigation.
context: Which transaction is unauthorized?
Refund you within 10 days if the transaction is confirmed as unauthorized

name: Complaint Handling Agent Script
description: A call centre script used by agents to document customer complaints, explain the escalation process to the Complaints Team, and provide timelines for resolution and external escalation options.
context: I'm sorry you've had a poor experience. We want to make this right. Let me document your complaint.
I'm escalating this to our Complaints Team. Here's what happens next:
If you disagree, you can escalate to the Financial Ombudsman Service (free and independent)

name: Complaint Reference Number
description: A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to a customer's complaint for tracking and record-keeping purposes.
context: Your complaint reference number is [EXC-XXXXX].

name: Complaint Investigation Timeline Obligation
description: The bank is obligated to investigate a customer complaint within a specific timeframe of 8 calendar days.
context: We'll investigate within 8 calendar days
We'll be in touch within 8 days.

name: Complaint Escalation Disclosure Obligation
description: Staff must inform the customer of their right to escalate the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service if they disagree with the bank's findings.
context: If you disagree, you can escalate to the Financial Ombudsman Service (free and independent)

name: Complaining Customer
description: A bank customer who is expressing dissatisfaction and initiating a formal complaint process.
context: Customer: "I want to file a complaint."
I'm sorry you've had a poor experience.

name: Standing Order Setup Agent Script
description: A call centre script used by agents to guide customers through the process of setting up a recurring standing order payment. It includes a data collection phase and a final confirmation step to ensure accuracy of payment details.
context: Agent: "Perfect! A standing order lets you set up recurring payments to anyone. Let me collect the details"
Let me confirm: - Paying [Recipient] £[amount] - Every [frequency] - Starting [date]

name: Recipient Name
description: The name of the person or entity to whom the standing order payments will be sent.
context: Who do you want to pay? (Recipient name)
Paying [Recipient]

name: Payment Amount
description: The specific monetary value to be transferred in each recurring payment cycle.
context: How much each time?
£[amount]

name: Payment Frequency
description: The interval at which the payment is repeated, such as weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annually.
context: How often? (Weekly, monthly, quarterly, annually)
Every [frequency]

name: Start Date
description: The calendar date on which the first standing order payment is scheduled to occur.
context: What date should it start?
Starting [date]

name: Recipient Bank Details
description: The account number and sort code of the recipient required to route the standing order payment.
context: Their bank details? (Account number and sort code)

name: Standing Order
description: A banking service that allows customers to set up automated, recurring payments to a specified recipient.
context: A standing order lets you set up recurring payments to anyone.

name: Scenario 7: Account Closure
description: A training scenario focused on the operational procedure for closing a customer account, including the agent's communication flow and the necessary administrative steps.
context: ## SCENARIO 7: Account Closure

name: Account Closure Agent Script
description: A structured script for agents to use when a customer requests to close their account. It covers the discovery of the reason for closure, explanation of the process, fund disbursement options, and a final retention attempt.
context: Agent: "I'm sorry to hear you want to close your account. Before you go, may I ask why? This helps us improve."
Let me explain the closure process:
Before I process this, are you sure you want to close? We'd love to keep you as a customer.
"I've processed your closure request. Your account will close in 5-7 days. We appreciate your business."

name: Customer requesting account closure
description: An existing bank customer who has initiated a request to terminate their banking relationship.
context: Customer: "I'd like to close my account."

name: Customer Account for Closure
description: The specific bank account being closed, which requires a final balance calculation and the cancellation of associated payment instructions.
context: I'd like to close my account.
calculate your final balance (including pending interest)

name: Standing Orders and Direct Debits
description: Recurring payment instructions linked to the account that must be cancelled as part of the closure workflow.
context: Cancel any standing orders or Direct Debits

name: Final Balance Transfer
description: The final movement of remaining funds from the closing account to the customer via bank transfer, cheque, or cash.
context: Transfer any remaining funds to your new bank
Transfer to another UK bank account (1-2 days)
Cheque in the post (3-5 days)
Cash in a branch (same day)

name: Account Closure Process Obligation
description: The mandatory operational steps that must be completed to successfully close a customer account, including balance calculation, instruction cancellation, and fund transfer.
context: 1. We'll calculate your final balance (including pending interest)
2. Cancel any standing orders or Direct Debits
3. Transfer any remaining funds to your new bank
4. Your account will be closed

name: Direct Debit Question Agent Script

context: Agent: "Let me look that up for you. A Direct Debit is when a company (like a utility or insurance) automatically deducts payment from your account."
If you didn't authorize it or want to cancel, I can help: Option 1: Cancel the Direct Debit with us (immediate) Option 2: Contact [Company] directly to cancel
Either way, if you were charged without authorization, we'll refund you within 10 days.
